title: Korean
description: Polite everyday Korean in Hangul with romanization: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: '안녕하세요' (annyeonghaseyo) is the everyday polite hello. For goodbye, say '안녕히 가세요' to someone who is leaving and '안녕히 계세요' to someone who is staying.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: 은/는 (eun/neun) after a noun marks the topic: 어머니는 (eomeonineun) = as for my mother. Koreans often say 우리 (our) for family: 우리 어머니.

units.title: Food and drink
tips: Objects take 을/를 (eul/reul) and the verb comes last: 커피를 마셔요 (keopireul masyeoyo) = (I) drink coffee.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: Korean has two sets of numbers. Native numbers (하나, 둘, 셋...) count things and tell the hour. Before a counter, 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네: 세 시 = three o'clock.

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: '어디예요?' (eodiyeyo) means 'where is it?'. Put the place first: 화장실이 어디예요?

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: Time and place words take 에 (e): 아침에 (achime) = in the morning, 학교에 (hakgyoe) = to school.

units.title: Shopping
units.description: Ask for things, prices and how to pay.
tips: '이거 주세요' (igeo juseyo, this one please) is all you need to buy something.

answers: Can I pay with a card?
